claim_boundary: C019 adds three descendants born from attacks on disconnectedness and positive-list compression. None resolves P versus NP or proves the remaining factorization theorem.

hypotheses.title: Connected Neutral-Bridge Toroidal Tseitin Twin Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: For every fixed signed-incidence radius R, add the same SAT-neutral five-clause bridge between charge-free edge variables in the two H121 toroidal components. The resulting SAT and UNSAT CNFs have connected primal graphs, opposite satisfiability, exact bounded-radius local equality by separated special neighborhoods, and primal treewidth at least m-1 for m=8R+13.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: The H121 obstruction no longer exposes disconnected input components as an immediate global side channel; identity compilation remains excluded by the inherited treewidth lower bound.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_TARGET: strengthen H121 by connecting its two high-treewidth lobes without changing semantics or bounded-radius local signatures.
hypotheses.next_gate: Obtain independent review of the separated-feature local-equality argument and then attack all low-treewidth transductions through H127.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H125 adds an explicit assignment-neutral bridge, makes the full primal graph connected, and preserves the H121 local and width guarantees by feature separation and subgraph monotonicity.
falsification_conditions: The bridge constrains an original endpoint assignment.
The SAT extension fails or the UNSAT base becomes satisfiable.
A radius-R neighborhood sees both a charge and the bridge, invalidating the separated-feature argument.
The bridged primal graph is disconnected or loses the inherited treewidth subgraph.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: The construction remains a restricted-locality target; connectedness does not prove the common-quotient theorem.

hypotheses.title: Exact-List SAT-Sound Cover Lemma Candidate
hypotheses.statement: For every finite set T of m distinct satisfiable formula encodings of exactly L bits, there is a globally SAT-sound Boolean circuit accepting exactly T with at most 3mL gates under a standard binary-gate accounting. Therefore any H124 list hitting every SAT-sound circuit of size L^k must contain more than L^(k-1)/3 distinct formulas, independently of witness diversity.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H124 must exceed both the H120 witness cover and the stronger exact-list membership cover; repeated formulas and merely diverse witnesses are insufficient.
hypotheses.proof_role: DIRECT_BRIDGE: expose the nonuniform exact-membership shadow automatically cast by every finite positive anti-checker list.
hypotheses.next_gate: Fix one canonical gate basis and encoding convention, then search for a uniform H124 generator producing enough distinct formulas while defeating semantic compression smaller than exact membership.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H126 removes witnesses from the covering attack: hardwired equality tests accept exactly the positive formula list and are sound solely because every listed formula is satisfiable.
falsification_conditions: An unlisted encoding accepted by the exact-membership circuit.
A listed formula rejected by its equality test.
A gate accounting requiring superlinear size per L-bit equality test.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: This is a necessary list-size bound, not a SAT circuit lower bound and not a refutation of H124.

hypotheses.title: Connected Toroidal Charge-Quotient Factorization Conjecture
hypotheses.statement: For every fixed-pass radius-bounded H106 transduction applied to the connected H125 pair, if both outputs have polynomial size and O(log n) primal treewidth, then the complete output and every recovery annotation factor through a common bounded quotient that is insensitive to whether the two unit charges lie in the same toroidal lobe or in different lobes. Hence no such transduction is equisatisfiable on both members.
hypotheses.consequence_if_true: H106 is refuted on a connected explicit high-treewidth family, eliminating identity compilation, disconnected-input branching, and purely local charge detection as escape routes.
hypotheses.proof_role: ADVERSARIAL_BRIDGE: restate H123 on the connected H125 target and isolate global quotient factorization as the only remaining locality theorem.
hypotheses.next_gate: Formalize H106 as an isomorphism-invariant finite transduction and either prove low-treewidth quotient factorization or construct a legal countertransduction preserving the lobe-parity bit.
hypotheses.delta_from_parents: H127 removes the disconnected-input premise from H123 while retaining the same explicit missing theorem for all output assembly and recovery data.
falsification_conditions: An H106-legal O(log n)-treewidth transduction that preserves same-lobe versus split-lobe charge parity on H125.
A recovery annotation carrying the parity bit without violating bounded ancestry.
Failure of the connected pair to share the required bounded-radius cover.
hypotheses.claim_boundary: No factorization theorem is proved. H127 attacks only the restricted H106 compiler model and does not imply P != NP by itself.
